pages.title: Accordion Component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-accordion component provides a collapsible content structure.
pages.body:
Accordion Component Breakdown Accordion Component Breakdown Overview The dd-accordion component provides a collapsible content structure. It leverages native HTML5 details and summary elements for accessibility and progressive enhancement, ensuring it works without JavaScript in modern browsers while allowing for JS enhancements. This component is ideal for FAQs, expandable sections, or grouped content. In WordPress, configure it via ACF repeater fields for accordion items (e.g., title and body). In Drupal, use a Paragraph type with fields for header and copy, rendered as a list of items. Basic Usage Wrap accordion items in a container with class dd-accordion. Each item uses details with a shared name attribute (e.g., "group1") to enforce exclusive opening (only one open at a time). The summary acts as the toggle, and the content follows in div with a class of class="dd-accordion__copy. Add spacers (e.g., div class="dd-spacer -xl") between items for visual separation if needed. pages.title: Alert Component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-alert component provides a flexible way to display notification messages, such as warnings, errors, successes, or informational alerts.

It supports different severity levels with color-coded visuals for quick user recognition. This component is ideal for form validation feedback, system messages, or user notifications. In WordPress, configure it via ACF fields for alert type, heading, and text. In Drupal, use a Paragraph type with select fields for type and text areas for content, allowing dynamic rendering based on conditions. Alternating Content Component Breakdown Alternating Content Component Breakdown Overview The dd-alternating component provides a layout for alternating content blocks, typically featuring an image on one side and text on the other, which switches sides for each subsequent item. This creates a visually engaging zigzag pattern, ideal for showcasing features, benefits, or narrative sections. This component is great for pages like "About Us," product features, or case studies. In WordPress, configure it via ACF repeater fields for alternating items (e.g., image, title, body, links). In Drupal, use a Paragraph type with fields for image and copy, rendered in a loop with alternating logic. Basic Usage Wrap items in a container with class dd-alternating and role="region" for accessibility. Each item contains a grid with image and copy columns that stack on mobile and side-by-side on larger screens. Use SAL attributes for fade animations. Preview Code

Alternating title

Alternating Link 2

The framework uses CSS :nth-child(odd/even) to alternate image/copy positions automatically. CSS Modifiers (from _dd_alternating.scss) The SCSS file defines base styles for the alternating layout, including responsive grid, spacing, and integration with SAL for animations. Key modifiers include: -reverse: Reverses the default alternating direction (e.g., starts with copy on left). -no-alternate: Disables alternating, keeping all items in the same order (image left, copy right). Utility classes for alignment. -x-center -y-center SAL data attributes for custom animations. data-sal="slide-up" For ACF/Paragraphs integration, use repeater sub-fields to generate items dynamically, with optional fields for custom modifiers. In CMS, validate image uploads for alt text requirements.

pages.title: Badge Component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-badge component is a compact, non-interactive pill used to communicate a status or severity level at a glance, such as critical, warning, info, or pass.
pages.body: Badge Component Breakdown Badge Component Breakdown Overview The dd-badge component is a compact, non-interactive pill used to communicate a status or severity level at a glance, such as critical, warning, info, or pass. Its colour-coded surface pairs with a short text label for fast, scannable recognition. This component is ideal for audit summaries, dashboards, and inline status indicators next to titles or table cells. In WordPress, configure it via ACF fields for severity and label. In Drupal, use a Paragraph type with a select field for severity and a text field for the label, allowing dynamic rendering based on data. Basic Usage Wrap the badge in a container with class dd-badge and place the visible text inside a dd-badge__label element. Apply a severity modifier such as -critical or omit it for the neutral variant. An optional dd-badge__icon may precede the label. Preview Code 🔴Critical ⚠️Warning ℹ️Info ✅Pass 14 tasks Use spacers or inline gaps when placing multiple badges in a row. CSS Modifiers (from _dd_badge.scss) The SCSS file defines the base pill shape, padding, and typography, with severity modifiers mapping to design tokens. Key modifiers include: -critical: Error tokens for the most severe status. -warning: Warning tokens for cautionary status. -info: Info tokens for neutral informational status. -pass: Success tokens for passing or healthy status. No modifier: Neutral variant using default surface tokens for unclassified status. Framework files source/scss/components/_dd_badge.scss (styles) Accessibility and Best Practices Meaning is carried by the dd-badge__label text, never by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Colour), so a badge remains understandable in greyscale or to colour-blind users. The optional dd-badge__icon is decorative and marked aria-hidden="true". The badge is non-interactive, so it takes no role, tabindex, or focus. Keep labels short and unambiguous, and ensure the surface and text colours meet WCAG AA contrast.

pages.title: Banner Component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-banner component provides a full-width banner image with customizable background positioning.
pages.body: Banner Component Breakdown Banner Component Breakdown Overview The dd-banner component provides a full-width banner image with customizable background positioning. It's designed for hero sections, promotional banners, or visual breaks, supporting responsive images and inline styles for background. This component is ideal for landing pages or section dividers. In WordPress, configure it via ACF fields for image upload, alt text, and position modifier. In Drupal, use a Paragraph type with image field and select list for background position, rendering the style attribute dynamically. Basic Usage Use a div with class dd-banner and data-sal for animations. Set background-image via inline style, with an img element for foreground or fallback, using srcset for responsiveness. Preview Code Add media queries in <style> for larger backgrounds. For overlays or text, nest content inside, as seen in header examples. CSS Modifiers (from _dd_banner.scss) The SCSS file defines base styles for the banner, including full-width, background sizing (cover/contain), and positioning utilities. Key modifiers include: -bg-top-left: Positions background at top-left. -bg-top-center: Positions at top-center. -bg-top-right: Positions at top-right. -bg-center-left: Positions at center-left. -bg-center-center: Positions at center-center (default if none specified). -bg-center-right: Positions at center-right. -bg-bottom-left: Positions at bottom-left. -bg-bottom-center: Positions at bottom-center. -bg-bottom-right: Positions at bottom-right. SAL data attributes for custom animations. data-sal="slide-up" Framework files source/js/vendors/sal.js (animations) source/scss/components/_dd_banner.scss (styles) Accessibility and Best Practices Provide descriptive alt text for images. If text overlays, ensure contrast ratios meet WCAG. Use aria-label for decorative banners. Test for keyboard focus if interactive. In CMS, enforce alt text requirements and validate image formats for responsiveness.

pages.title: Data Table Component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-data-table component is an accessible table with a caption, scoped header cells, and optional status cells that embed the dd-badge component.
pages.body:
Data Table Component Breakdown Data Table Component Breakdown Overview The dd-data-table component is an accessible table with a caption, scoped header cells, and optional status cells that embed the dd-badge component. It wraps the table in a keyboard-focusable horizontal scroll region and supports optional column sorting and an empty state. This component is ideal for report data, comparison grids, and audit result listings. In WordPress, configure it via a repeater of rows and a header definition, with a status column mapped to badge severities. In Drupal, use a Views table or a Paragraph type with structured field data. Basic Usage Wrap a semantic with a
and
headers inside the dd-data-table container. Status cells embed a dd-badge, and sortable columns use native header buttons. The scroll region and sorting behaviour are wired up by the component JS. Preview Code
Prioritized remediation tasks
ID Finding
SEO-001 Critical Missing <title> tag 2h
SEO-002 Warning Thin meta description 1h
Provide an empty state row when there is no data to display. CSS Modifiers (from _dd_data_table.scss) The SCSS file defines the table layout, cell padding, scroll region, and focus styling. Key modifiers include: -dense: Reduces cell padding for compact, data-heavy tables. No modifier: Default comfortable spacing for standard readability. Framework files source/js/components/_dd_data_table.js (scroll region and sort) source/scss/components/_dd_data_table.scss (styles) Accessibility and Best Practices The
names the table, and header cells use
for correct association. The scroll region receives tabindex="0", role="region", and an aria-label from the JS only when it actually overflows, so keyboard users can scroll without adding an empty tab stop otherwise. The focus ring uses a high-contrast dark colour rather than the brand green so it stays visible on all cell backgrounds.

An accent stripe reinforces the severity for quick visual scanning. This component is ideal for accessibility, SEO, and security audit reports where issues need to be listed with clear priority. In WordPress, configure it via a repeater of findings with severity, title, evidence, and fix fields. In Drupal, use a Paragraph type with a select for severity and text areas for evidence and fix. Basic Usage Wrap the findings in a dd-finding list, using
    when the order communicates priority or
      when it does not. Each dd-finding__item holds a severity dd-badge, a title heading, and optional evidence and fix blocks. Apply the matching stripe modifier per item. Preview Code

      Priority findings

      1. Critical

        Missing <title> tag

        No <title> in <head>.

        Fix: Add a unique 50–60 char title.

      2. Info

        Striking-distance query ‘web design’ at position 12

        4,200 impressions, 0.8% CTR.

        Fix: Strengthen on-page relevance and internal links.

      3. Pass

        Canonical tags present on all pages

      Order findings by severity when using the ordered list form. Key modifiers include: -critical: Error-toned accent stripe for critical findings. -warning: Warning-toned accent stripe for warnings. -info: Info-toned accent stripe for informational notes. -pass: Success-toned accent stripe for passing checks.         or

pages.title: Modal Component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-modal component provides a dialog-based modal window for displaying content overlays.
pages.body:
Modal Component Breakdown Modal Component Breakdown Overview The dd-modal component provides a dialog-based modal window for displaying content overlays. It uses the native HTML5 dialog element for built-in accessibility and focus management, ensuring it works progressively with or without JavaScript enhancements. This component is ideal for alerts, forms, confirmations, or additional content displays. In WordPress, configure it via ACF fields for modal triggers and content. In Drupal, use Paragraphs with fields for button text, modal content, and IDs. Basic Usage Use buttons with data-modal-open and data-id attributes to open modals. The modal itself uses dialog with data-modal and a matching id. Include a close button with data-modal-close and data-id inside the modal. Preview Code

Framework files source/js/_dd_modal.js (animations) source/scss/components/_dd_modal.scss (styles) Accessibility and Best Practices The dialog element provides automatic focus management and keyboard navigation (ESC to close). Ensure close buttons have proper aria-label. Test with screen readers. In CMS, ensure modal content is meaningful and avoid nesting interactive elements.

pages.title: Score Ring Component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-score-ring component is a radial SVG donut gauge that displays a score against a maximum, with a visible number and a short label.
pages.body:
Score Ring Component Breakdown Score Ring Component Breakdown Overview The dd-score-ring component is a radial SVG donut gauge that displays a score against a maximum, with a visible number and a short label. An arc sweeps proportionally to the value to give an immediate sense of how full or complete a score is. This component is ideal for audit scores, health indicators, and KPI summaries, and it supports an optional link form so the whole gauge can navigate to a detail view. In WordPress, configure it via ACF fields for score, max, tone, and an optional URL. In Drupal, use a Paragraph type with number fields for score and max plus a select for tone. Basic Usage Wrap the gauge in a container with class dd-score-ring containing an inline SVG for the arc, a visible number, and a dd-score-ring__label. Use the figure form for a static gauge or the -link anchor form to make it navigable. Preview Code
Performance
13 checks
On-Page
Security
View details
 Group multiple rings in a grid to compare scores side by side. CSS Modifiers (from _dd_score_ring.scss) The SCSS file defines the ring geometry, arc stroke, and typography, with size and tone modifiers driven by design tokens. Key modifiers include: -sm: Small size for dense layouts. -lg: Large size for feature or hero placement. -good: Success-toned arc for healthy scores. -warn: Warning-toned arc for middling scores. -bad: Error-toned arc for poor scores. -link: Renders the anchor form so the whole gauge is navigable. Framework files source/scss/components/_dd_score_ring.scss (styles) Accessibility and Best Practices In the figure form the SVG carries role="img" and an aria-label stating the score and maximum. In the link form the owns the accessible name and the SVG is marked aria-hidden="true" to avoid a duplicate announcement. The value is always present as visible text, so meaning does not depend on the arc or colour (WCAG 1.1.1 and 1.4.1). The arc grow-in animation is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion, and the link hit area is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum).

pages.title: Section Component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-section component provides a foundational container for grouping content blocks on a page.
pages.body:
Section Component Breakdown Section Component Breakdown Overview The dd-section component provides a foundational container for grouping content blocks on a page. It handles layout constraints, background colors (with alternation), padding, and responsive widths, serving as a wrapper for other components like titles, grids, and items. This component is ideal for dividing pages into logical sections, such as intros, features, or footers. In WordPress, configure it via ACF flexible content or layouts for section types, with fields for full/contained, title, and inner items. In Drupal, use a Paragraph type as a section wrapper, nesting other paragraphs inside, with options for modifiers. Basic Usage Use a section with class dd-section for contained width or add -full for full-width. Include content with title and items in a grid. Backgrounds alternate automatically via CSS. Preview Code

Nest other components inside __items for modular builds; use l-box for padding on items. CSS Modifiers (from _dd_section.scss) The SCSS file defines base styles for sections, including default padding, max-width, and alternating backgrounds via :nth-child. Key modifiers include: -full: Sets max-width to 100% for full-width sections (apply to both section and __content). -contained: Limits __content to a max-width (default behavior; explicit for overrides). -no-padding: Removes default padding for custom spacing. Utility classes for alignment. -x-center -y-center SAL data attributes for custom animations. data-sal="slide-up" Framework files source/scss/components/_dd_section.scss (styles) For ACF/Paragraphs integration, use conditional fields to apply modifiers dynamically. Accessibility and Best Practices Use role="region" and aria-labelledby for titled sections. Ensure backgrounds provide sufficient contrast. Nest semantic elements inside. Test landmark navigation with screen readers. In CMS, make titles optional but encouraged for labeled regions.

pages.title: Spacer component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-spacer component provides a simple way to add vertical spacing or dividers between elements, helping control layout flow without custom CSS.
pages.body:
Spacer component Breakdown Spacer component Breakdown Overview The dd-spacer component provides a simple way to add vertical spacing or dividers between elements, helping control layout flow without custom CSS. It supports predefined sizes and an optional divider line, making it a utility for consistent padding in sections, grids, or between components. This component is ideal for adding breathing room in content-heavy areas or separating blocks visually. In WordPress, configure it via an ACF select field for size and divider options within flexible content. In Drupal, use a Paragraph type with a select field for size and a boolean for divider, rendering as a standalone element. Basic Usage Use a div with class dd-spacer and a size modifier like -xl. Add -divider for a horizontal line.
Place it between elements or sections for spacing; it's full-width by default and can be nested in grids or sections. Preview Code
CSS Modifiers (from _dd_spacer.scss) The SCSS file defines base styles for the spacer as a block element with relative positioning and 100% width. Key modifiers include: -sm: Adds 0.5rem top/bottom margin. -md: Adds 1rem top/bottom margin. -lg: Adds 1.5rem top/bottom margin. -xl: Adds 2rem top/bottom margin. -xxl: Adds 2.5rem top/bottom margin. -xxxl: Adds 3rem top/bottom margin. -divider: Adds a 1px solid border (colored via primary variable). For ACF/Paragraphs integration, use select fields to apply size and divider classes dynamically. Framework files source/scss/components/_dd_spacer.scss (styles) Accessibility and Best Practices Avoid overusing spacers; prefer semantic spacing via CSS margins/padding. For dividers, ensure they don't create empty landmarks. Use aria-hidden if decorative. Test for consistent flow in screen readers. In CMS, limit options to predefined sizes for design consistency and prevent abuse.

pages.title: Tabs Component Breakdown
pages.description: The dd-tabs component provides a tabbed interface for organizing content into switchable panels.
pages.body:
Tabs Component Breakdown Tabs Component Breakdown Overview The dd-tabs component provides a tabbed interface for organizing content into switchable panels. It supports desktop navigation and a mobile dropdown menu, with ARIA attributes for accessibility, making it suitable for FAQs, product details, or multi-section content without page reloads. This component is ideal for content-heavy pages where space-saving is key. In WordPress, configure it via ACF repeater fields for tab items (e.g., label, content, links). In Drupal, use a Paragraph type with fields for tab titles and bodies, rendered with unique data-id for scoping multiple instances. Basic Usage Wrap tabs in a div with class dd-tabs and a unique data-id. Include navigation with menu items (ARIA roles) and content panels with aria-hidden and role="tabpanel". Preview Code
  • open tab 1
  • open tab 2
  • open tab 3

tab panel 001

tab panel 002

tab panel 003

Use unique IDs for tabs and panels; JS handles switching and mobile toggle. CSS Modifiers (from _dd_tabs.scss) The SCSS file defines base styles for tabs, including responsive navigation (hidden menu on mobile), active states, and overflow handling. Key modifiers include: -active: Applied to active menu items and panels for visibility and styling. -horizontal: Adjusts for horizontal tab layouts if extended. -vertical: For vertical tab orientations (sidebar style). Utility classes like SAL data attributes (e.g., data-sal="fade") for panel animations. Associated JavaScript (from dd_tabs.js) The component includes a JS file handling mobile menu toggle and tab switching with ARIA updates. Key features: Toggles -active class on mobile menu open/close. Switches tabs on click, updating aria-selected, aria-hidden, and active classes, scoped by aria-controls. Updates mobile placeholder text to current tab label. Supports multiple tab groups on a page via aria-controls and panel ID. Include the JS via your CMS: In WordPress, enqueue in functions.php; in Drupal, attach via libraries.yml. For ACF/Paragraphs integration, generate unique aria-controls from fields. Framework files source/js/components/_dd_tabs.js (javascript) source/scss/components/_dd_tabs.scss (styles) Accessibility and Best Practices Use ARIA roles (tablist, tab, tabpanel) and attributes (aria-selected, aria-controls, aria-labelledby, aria-hidden). Ensure keyboard navigation (focus on tabs, enter/space to activate). Test with screen readers for announcements. In CMS, require unique labels and validate content for empty panels.

pages.title: Grid
pages.description: The dd-grid component provides a responsive 24-column grid system based on flexbox, enabling flexible layouts for rows and columns with utilities for...
pages.body:
Grid Grid Overview The dd-grid component provides a responsive 24-column grid system based on flexbox, enabling flexible layouts for rows and columns with utilities for alignment, spacing, and responsive breakpoints. It's the foundational layout tool for arranging content blocks, supporting full-width, contained, and nested grids. This component is essential for all pages, used in sections, cards, tabs, and more. In WordPress, integrate it via ACF layouts or groups to define grid structures dynamically. In Drupal, use it within Paragraph templates for entity rendering, with classes applied via field formatters or preprocess functions. Basic Usage Wrap grid items in a div with class dd-g for the row. Use column classes like dd-u-*-24 for widths, with breakpoints (xs, sm, md, lg, xl, etc.). Add l-box for item padding. For responsive: dd-u-md-12-24 for 50% on medium and up, full-width below. CSS Modifiers (from _grid.scss) The SCSS file defines the grid with flexbox, no-gutters option, and responsive utilities up to x4k breakpoints. Key modifiers include: -x-center, -y-center: Justify/align content (from modifiers.scss). Breakpoint-specific: xs (default), sm, md, lg, xl, xxl, xxxl, x4k for media queries. For ACF/Paragraphs integration, apply grid classes dynamically based on field choices. Accessibility and Best Practices Use semantic elements inside grids (e.g., role="row" for data grids). Ensure logical tab order. For tables, prefer semantic over grids. Test responsive reflow for readability. In CMS, provide field options for column spans and validate for mobile-first designs.
